findings.finding: Some Dubai real estate agents are experiencing reduced deal flow, spending more time discussing potential deals rather than closing them.
findings.qualification: This is self-reported, so it may not reflect broader industry trends.

findings.finding: Changes have been made to Dubai's 2-year property owner visa to enhance its real estate market.
findings.qualification: The specific details of these changes and their impacts remain unverified.

findings.finding: Over recent months, some rental deals in Dubai have been closed at prices 20% below market value.
findings.qualification: The scope and prevalence of this trend across the market are uncertain.

findings.finding: AI voice solutions in domain of PropTech are currently not being actively adopted in Dubai's real estate market.
findings.qualification: This observation might not encompass all PropTech solutions or market segments.

findings.finding: In Dubai's past real estate downturn around 2008, property prices dropped nearly 50% in less than a year, driven by high credit dependency.
findings.qualification: This historical context is descriptive of past events; current market conditions differ.

findings.finding: Currently, the majority of real estate transactions in Dubai are cash-based due to restrictions on mortgage lending.
findings.qualification: This trend is suggested but not confirmed with broad data.

findings.finding: There is acknowledgment of ongoing risks in Dubai's real estate market, though they differ from those of the 2008 crisis.
findings.qualification: It is a belief self-reported by an observer, not a definitive market analysis.
